title: Smoke in the Cockpit
tagline: Smoke from behind the panels at FL220 over the Channel.
history: Inspired by in-flight fires that spread behind cockpit and cabin linings — a 1998 accident over the sea above all — after which the industry's guidance became: get the aircraft on the ground, as fast as possible.
situation: Thirty miles south-west of Lydd at FL220, heading out over the Channel with 96 aboard. There's an acrid smell, then smoke from behind the overhead panel. Nobody can say where the fire is. You have about 16 minutes.
failures: Electrical smoke / fire behind the panels — it will not stay isolated
The fire becomes uncontrollable in about 16 minutes
tips: Turn back now: Lydd (runway 03/21, 1,505 m) is behind you
Emergency descent: thrust idle, speed brakes, high speed
Don't fly a long pattern — a short, steep, stable approach
limit_text: The fire burned through the cockpit before you could land.

do.note: Captain: Do you smell that? … Smoke. It's coming from the overhead.
Purser: There's smoke in the forward cabin now, and the ceiling is hot to touch.
F/O: It's back — and thicker. Isolating didn't hold it.

objectives.text: Start down: speed brakes within 90 s
Land and stop before the fire takes hold
